This is the same process that has guided all of our other academy decisions ensuring fairness transparency and consistency across the division. We held a dedicated session with all high school principals to walk through the Army ROTC program.

During that session, we covered the program goals, expectations, and what hosting would entail. High school principals then received an interest form and had until close of business on February 13th to indicate whether they wished to be considered as a host site.

A committee then reviewed all submissions using a clear set of criteria. The goal was to identify the school best position to support the academy's success. The school decision was guided by a thorough assessment of four key criteria. Community alignment, ensuring the academy is placed where community interest and demographic data show strong support and relevance.

Leadership commitment, confirming that school leadership not only expressed interest but demonstrated readiness to champion and sustain the program. Building capacity, verifying that the school has the space. Staffing flexibility and infrastructure to host the academy without compromising existing programs.

And then lastly, transportation and accessibility, selecting a location that provides reasonable access for students across the division. With that, we are happy to announce that the school selected was Stonebridge High School.
